title: Representation and Expansion of Overridden vs Excluded Recurrence Instances

citations.verbatim_quote:
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
   BEGIN:VEVENT
   UID:F4257E1D-5461-4EF6-840F-9DFC653EB559
   RRULE:FREQ=DAILY
   DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240101T140000
   ...
   END:VEVENT
   BEGIN:VEVENT
   UID:F4257E1D-5461-4EF6-840F-9DFC653EB559
   RECURRENCE-ID;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240202T140000
   DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20240202T160000

The entries in the "recurrenceOverrides" property convert depending on the contents of the PatchObject value. A PatchObject that sets the "excluded" member to "true" converts to an EXDATE property for the date-time of that recurrence instance. An empty PatchObject converts to an RDATE property. Any other PatchObject converts to a recurrence override component in the embedding VCALENDAR component.

If the patch object defines the "excluded" property of an occurrence to be true, this occurrence is omitted from the final set of recurrences for the calendar object (like an EXDATE from iCalendar). Such a patch object MUST NOT patch any other property. By default, an occurrence inherits all properties from the main object except the start (or due) date-time, which is shifted to match the recurrence id LocalDateTime. However, individual properties of the occurrence can be modified by a patch or multiple patches.

rationale: RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4, RFC 5546 Section 4.4.8, RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5, and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Sections 2.1.2 and 3.2 establish a strict partitioning between an excluded recurrence instance and an overridden (modified) recurrence instance: (1) An excluded instance (`excluded: true` in JSCalendar) is omitted from the recurrence expansion and is represented in iCalendar by an EXDATE property on the main recurring component with no override component. (2) An overridden instance (a property modification PatchObject in JSCalendar) remains part of the recurrence set and is represented in iCalendar by a sibling VEVENT or VTODO component sharing the same UID and specifying RECURRENCE-ID equal to the original occurrence start time, without requiring an EXDATE on the main component. During recurrence expansion, the override component replaces the main component's generated occurrence whose original start time matches RECURRENCE-ID.
store_implication:
1. Recurrence expansion MUST treat a sibling component with RECURRENCE-ID as replacing the corresponding occurrence generated by the main component (matching by UID and normalized RECURRENCE-ID instant), emitting the override instance in place of the main component's candidate occurrence without requiring an EXDATE on the main component.
2. Calendar store operations MUST preserve the semantic distinction between an overridden instance (a modified occurrence represented by a RECURRENCE-ID component) and an excluded instance (a deleted occurrence represented by an EXDATE on the main component): an overridden instance MUST NOT be treated as a deleted occurrence during subsequent series-wide edits, THISANDFUTURE range splits/deletions, or single-instance lookups.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: An iCalendar stream containing a main recurring component (without EXDATE) and a sibling override component with RECURRENCE-ID: timeline expansion MUST replace the original occurrence with the override component so that the slot is emitted once (with the override's properties and rescheduled DTSTART), never twice.

If a main component has an override component at RECURRENCE-ID T, a subsequent series-wide edit or THISANDFUTURE operation targeting T or earlier MUST still recognize T as part of the series rather than failing to find the main series or turning the overridden occurrence into a permanently excluded (deleted) slot.

When resolving a specific recurrence_id T where both a main recurring component and an override component with RECURRENCE-ID=T exist in the calendar, single-instance operations (Range=NONE) MUST target the override component for T rather than forking a second override component from the main component.

scenarios.name: single_instance_edit_replaces_occurrence_on_timeline
scenarios.description: Editing one instance of a 3-occurrence series creates a RECURRENCE-ID override component that replaces the corresponding master occurrence on the timeline, yielding 3 total occurrences (2 from the main component, 1 from the override).
